title: Weekly Clarity Anchor: commitments & micro-experiments
content:
Purpose
Set an explicit, compact checkpoint to keep day-to-day work tied to outcomes (not just tickets). Use short experiments to surface friction early and make 1% measurable improvements to throughput and focus.

Week snapshot (Mar 8 - Mar 14, 2026)
- High-level outcome: Reduce queuing latency on inference staging by 12% for 8-token priming sequences (customer-sim testing).
- Why this week: We have 2 customers hitting sudden tail latency and it's adding to SLO risk. If I can knock down median queuing by ~10–15% with a config/ops tweak + a small batching policy change, we can avoid an ops escalation.

Signals I care about (leading/lagging)
- Leading: avg queue time at router for 1–8 tokens (per model variant) — goal: 10% down from baseline 28ms -> target ~25ms.
- Lagging: 95th percentile end-to-end latency on staging harness for customer scenario — goal: <240ms.
- Side signals: number of stale KV-cache reuse events, CPU steal during bursts, error rates during autoscale.

What I shipped last week (quick wins)
- Small router change: lowered max batching window by 5ms for small seqs (AB test v21). Observed median queue down 4ms in canary.
- Ran a smoke eval with customer traces (10k requests) — found one model variant spikes when burst concurrency > 120. Filed PLAT-8742.

Hypotheses + micro-experiments this week (ranked)
1) Hypothesis: aggressively favor small-window batch assembly for <12-token requests reduces per-request queue time without hurting throughput.
   Experiment: deploy batcher policy beta-3 to two nodes in staging for 48 hours, 20% traffic. Measure median queue time and tokens/sec.
   Success metric: median queue time <= -8% and tokens/sec drop <= 3%.
   Confounding: if request size distribution shifts (more 32-token requests), batching overhead shifts.

2) Hypothesis: enabling light quantized-kv-cache (8-bit) on the variant reduces memory pressure and lowers CPU swap/steal during peaks, improving tail latency.
   Experiment: spin dedicated small-node pool (beta quant-kv) and run the 10k trace.
   Success metric: 95th percentile latency improves by 10–12% vs baseline.

3) Hypothesis: small changes to routing priority (preferring dedicated reserved pool for seen-client tokens) reduces cross-tenant interference.
   Experiment: short canary of priority flag on 5 reserved sessions, monitor error/queue delta.

Quick action list (this doc is my sprint anchor)
- [ ] Kick off batcher-policy deploy to staging (assign: me) — blocked until infra slot opens (SRE ticket).
- [ ] Add monitoring panel: "queue_time_small_seq" with per-model variant breakdown (assign: Leila).
- [ ] Run 10k customer trace on beta quant-kv pool (assign: Arjun).
- [ ] Draft short blurb for customer success: what we are testing and expected timelines (assign: me).

Risks & mitigations
- Risk: regressions in throughput. Mitigate by incremental 20% traffic ramp and clear rollback.
- Risk: config churn adds noise to metrics. Mitigate by locking unrelated config changes for 72h of experiment.

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep runbooks ready; if 95th latency > 320ms during experiment, rollback immediately.
- Talk to SRE before the deploy — remember they prefer deploy windows 10–12 PST on weekdays.
- This is a test of trade-offs: small improvements in short sequences can sometimes increase batching inefficiency for medium sequences. Visualize distribution.

Reflection questions for Friday retro
- Did we see consistent improvement across >3 independent runs? If not, what changed between runs?
- What was the smallest change that delivered measurable impact? Can that be automated?
- Did the experiment surface a new monitoring gap? (If yes, add to backlog)

Personal throughput commitments (micro habits this week)
- 3 focused 90-minute blocks: two for experiments, one for customer comms and doc updates.
- Daily 15-min morning note: record expectation vs observed for the day (quick).

Meeting / calendar nudges
- 2026-03-09 11:00 PT: sync w/Leila (add panel + instrumentation).
- 2026-03-10 16:00 PT: SRE window check; request deployment slot.
- 2026-03-12 09:00 PT: quick demo of initial canary numbers for product ops.

Unresolved questions (to chase)
- Is there a quick way to export per-request KV-cache reuse counts from the runtime? (Who to ask: Tara in serving-runtime)
- Can we run the 10k trace with TLS disabled to eliminate decryption CPU as a variable for the test? (ask infra/security)

End-of-week micro-retro template (fill Friday)
- What worked (one line):
- What did not (one line):
- One small improvement for next week: (one line)
- Blockers carried forward: (short list)

Scratch: quick metric snapshot (paste from Grafana when available)
- baseline_median_queue_small_seq: 28ms
- current_median_queue_small_seq: 22ms (after last change)
- staging_95th_latency_customer_trace: 248ms

Last note: keep outcome narrow and measurable. I tend to chase efficiency tricks; this week the goal is to be conservative with changes and heavily instrument everything.
